story: A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted Chinese telecom company Huawei on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, while acquitting it of racketeering.
title: Brooklyn jury convicts Huawei of fraud and trade-secret theft
dek: A federal jury convicted Huawei of bank fraud and conspiracy to steal trade secrets but acquitted it of racketeering after a three-month trial.
body:
A federal jury in Brooklyn found the Chinese telecommunications company Huawei and three subsidiaries guilty on Tuesday of ten criminal counts. Those include bank fraud, wire fraud, money-laundering conspiracy, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets. The jury acquitted the companies of racketeering conspiracy and of conspiring to obstruct justice.

The case was heard in the Eastern District of New York after a three-month trial. Prosecutors argued that Huawei spent more than two decades taking technology from US competitors and concealing work in Iran so banks would continue clearing its dollar payments. The Justice Department said the evidence included an employee leaving a T-Mobile laboratory with part of a secret testing robot, known as Tappy, in a backpack. Engineers were also said to have copied Cisco router code and left notes calling the original “ocsic” — Cisco spelled backwards. Further examples concerned antenna designs and semiconductor hardware. On Iran, officials said Huawei ran business through a subsidiary called Skycom while telling banks it was only an independent partner, and that it supplied equipment and tools used to monitor and censor users.

Huawei’s lawyer, Brian Heberlig, called the racketeering acquittal a profound rejection of the claim that the firm was corrupt from top to bottom. The company said the other charges lack legal or factual merit, described the trade-secret matters as old civil disputes that had been settled, and announced it would appeal. No individual executives were tried. Related charges against chief financial officer Meng Wanzhou were dropped in 2021 after she returned to China following nearly three years of restrictions in Canada.

Sentencing is set for 14 September 2027. The firms face fines, forfeiture and restitution. Reports have suggested the sums could reach into the billions, though a judge will decide. Huawei has been barred from selling gear to US carriers since 2019, and several allies have limited its 5G role. It has continued a substantial business elsewhere. In Switzerland, Sunrise has maintained a long supply partnership with the company, so questions about which equipment stays in local networks are not abstract.

The split verdict gives each side a point to stress. A US jury, after hearing the evidence, found specific acts of fraud and theft proved. It did not accept the broader picture of the company as a criminal enterprise. Appeals will test those findings, and the financial cost is still unknown. Some of the details that reached the jury — a badge reading “Weihua,” source code tagged with a reversed brand name — were not models of careful disguise. Courtrooms measure such things one exhibit at a time, which is slower than a press release and, on the evidence presented here, more precise.
